$comment: THE ENTRY-SCRIPT GATE. `checkJs` over the plain-JavaScript files that START things.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `start-ui.mjs` shipped a line referencing WEDGE_PORT with
no import and no definition. It was invisible to `npm run typecheck` because
the root tsconfig includes only `*.ts` -- and every verification of it passed,
because the shell running the verification had WEDGE_PORT set, so the `??`
short-circuited before the bare reference was evaluated. With a stripped
environment it was a ReferenceError.
So the bug was statically visible the whole time. Nothing was looking. This
file is the looking.
NO NEW DEPENDENCY. typescript is already a devDependency for the kernel gate;
this reuses the same binary with different flags. Per the mandate, an ADR is
required only if a dependency is added, and none is -- the change is two
compiler flags and a script entry.
WHY `noEmit` AND `noImplicitAny: false`. These files are deliberately plain
JavaScript with no annotations. Turning on `noImplicitAny` would demand
annotations across every entry script and produce noise that hides the one
error that matters. `noUnusedLocals` is OFF for the same reason: an unused
import in a start script is a lint opinion, not a defect.
WHAT IT CATCHES: undeclared identifiers, misspelled imports, wrong arity on an
imported function, and typos in property names on typed values. What it does
NOT catch is anything about runtime behaviour; that is what the tests and the
stripped-environment spawn in `platform/core/entry-contract.test.ts` are for.
